### 3. bl-0044

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Confirmed. `RopeBackend.initialize` (`src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/rope_backend.py:243-258`) calls `AutoImport(project, memory=True).generate_cache()` at startup. In rope 1.14.0, `generate_cache` (`.venv/Lib/site-packages/rope/contrib/autoimport/sqlite.py:373-402`) always runs `with ProcessPoolExecutor():` (`:394`) with default `max_workers` (CPU count) and has no single-process option. The lazy fallback in `autoimport_search` (`rope_backend.py:1251-1259`) calls the same `generate_cache`, so the first search would also spawn the pool. Making it lazy alone moves the orphan risk instead of removing it. `generate_modules_cache` has `single_thread` (`sqlite.py:404-452`) but it indexes external modules, not project files. Public `update_resource` (`sqlite.py:536-545`) indexes one project file in-process: `get_names` + `_add_name`, no pool. |
| Approach | Chosen fix: a lazy build that runs in-process. (1) Delete the pre-warm block at `rope_backend.py:243-258`, so `initialize` only opens the `Project`. (2) Add a private `_build_autoimport(project)` helper. It creates `AutoImport(project, memory=True)`, calls `update_resource(res, commit=False)` for each `project.get_python_files()`, then `autoimport.connection.commit()`, and closes the AutoImport if any step raises. (3) Replace `generate_cache()` in the lazy branch of `autoimport_search` (`:1253-1259`) with this helper. Keep the existing `_autoimport_lock` and `close()` ownership. Why this over the alternatives: a lazy build still spawns the pool through `generate_cache`. Skipping only the analysis profile does not work, because `autoimport_search` is read-only and is advertised in BOTH profiles (`tool_registry.py:1679`, refactoring support set). A bounded `max_workers` needs a rope patch or a monkeypatch of rope's module global. With no pool, nothing needs shutdown on EOF, so Acceptance bullet 2 is moot. The helper uses only public rope API (`update_resource`, `connection`). |
| Scope | Production 1: `src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/rope_backend.py`. Tests 1 extended: `tests/unit/test_rope_backend.py`. Fragment `changelog.d/fixed-bl-0044.md`. Inside the Rule 3/4 targets; no exemption. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |
| Estimated context cost | 25000 |
| Risks | The first `autoimport_search` on a large workspace now indexes serially inside the 30s `_DEFAULT_ROPE_TIMEOUT` (`rope_backend.py:74`). If it times out, the build thread keeps holding `_autoimport_lock` until it finishes. Accepted: before this fix it had the same timeout, plus the spawn cost. The in-memory DB is fresh, so the `delete_by_package_name` step in `generate_cache` is not needed. The shared file `rope_backend.py` (hotspot) overlaps sibling bl-0035 (change-stack code, a different region). That is a conflict-graph edge, not a dependency. Fanout: not refactor-shaped (no signature or contract change), so fanoutEstimate is null. No bundle peers. The docs "pre-warm" mentions (`docs/setup.md:90`, `ai_docs/runtime.md:66`) are about the workspace pre-warm, not AutoImport, and are unaffected. |
| Validation | New test: monkeypatch `rope.contrib.autoimport.sqlite.ProcessPoolExecutor` to raise, then assert that `initialize()` leaves `_autoimport is None` and that `autoimport_search("add")` still returns `("from calc import add", "add")` (mirror `test_rope_backend.py:417-423`). Existing `test_autoimport_search_*` stay green. `just ci`. |
| Performance review | Startup gets faster (no process pool). The first `autoimport_search` indexes project files serially in-process; later calls hit the cached DB. No other hot path. |
| CHANGELOG category | Fixed |
| CHANGELOG entry (draft) | - **Fixed:** Rope AutoImport no longer pre-warms at startup through a CPU-wide process pool that left orphaned `spawn_main` workers when the server was killed; the cache is now built lazily and in-process on the first `autoimport_search`. |
| Backlog sync | Close rows: [bl-0044]. |

### 11. bl-0041

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Confirmed. `util/shared.py:121` `Path(file_path).resolve()` anchors a relative path at the server cwd. Worse, workspace SELECTION happens first: `tool_runtime.py:282` `_resolve_backends` -> `workspace_registry.py:124` `Path(file_path).resolve()` picks (and may lazily initialize) a workspace from the cwd-relative path before `_validate_params` (`tool_runtime.py:286`) runs. `output_dir` (bl-0026) anchors at the workspace (`tool_runtime.py:176-181`, `type_stubs.py:42-50`) only because it never selects the workspace (comment `tool_runtime.py:42-46`). |
| Approach | DECISION: reject relative `file_path`/`root_path` (all `PATH_PARAMS`, `file_paths`, transaction-step `file_path`) with `[INVALID_INPUT]`; do NOT resolve against the workspace. Rationale: (1) circular - these params choose the workspace (`tool_runtime.py:135-153`), so no workspace exists to anchor them in multi-workspace mode; `output_dir` is not comparable, it follows an already-chosen workspace. (2) Documented contract already says absolute: `tool_params.py:26,28,44,47,72`. (3) MCP tool args carry no server cwd; client roots are absolute `file://` URIs. Edits: `shared.py` `validate_workspace_path` raises `ToolInputError` for a non-absolute input (defense for direct callers); `tool_runtime.py` add `_reject_relative_paths(kwargs)` called in `tool_error_boundary` BEFORE `_resolve_backends`, message names the param (`validate_identifier` label style, `shared.py:101-112`). `~/x` counts as relative; on Windows a POSIX-rooted `/x` is not absolute and is rejected (pin in a test). DIR_PARAMS pass an absolute candidate, unaffected. The rejection covers every `PATH_PARAMS` entry (`tool_runtime.py:32-39`), so the three undocumented ones get an absolute contract too: add described aliases `SourcePath`, `DestinationFile`, `DestinationPackage` ("Absolute path …") in `tool_params.py` following its alias pattern and retype `move_symbol.destination_file` (`tool_registry.py:627`) and `move_module.source_path`/`destination_package` (`:1193-1194`). PR body lists all 7 affected params in the breaking callout. |
| Scope | Production 4: `src/python_refactor_mcp/util/shared.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_runtime.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_params.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_registry.py` (within the 4-file target; the rejection would make the 3 bare-`str` descriptions silently incomplete, so they move with the behavior). Tests 1: `tests/unit/test_error_boundary.py` (extend). Fragment `changelog.d/changed-breaking-bl-0041.md`. No deletions. |

| Estimated context cost | 30000 |

Probe: `validate_workspace_path` has callers in 2 prod files (`tool_runtime.py:167,174,181,186`, `type_stubs.py:50`), both pass absolute paths except PATH_PARAMS; signature unchanged. Existing tests pass absolute `tmp_path` paths. bl-0042 (dep on this) owns the DIR_PARAMS/`_resolve_stub_root` helper share - do not absorb.
